lines.text: Hi, I'm Sindy! Let's open the cluster configuration file.
Do your tests need more than the defaults? More nodes, a database, users, or your own Slurm settings: one YAML file describes it all.
The smallest config is a single line: kind Cluster.
sind fills in the rest: the name default, the image of your sind release, one CPU and five hundred twelve megabytes per node, and a controller with one worker.
A bigger config uses more sections. The defaults section applies to every node, unless the node sets its own value.
The storage section sets up the shared data directory, here as a Docker volume.
The groups, users and accounts sections add Linux users and Slurm accounts.
Careful, though: a config is as trusted as a script. It can run any image and mount any host directory.
The slurm section adds your own lines to the generated configuration.
And the nodes section lists the roles: a bigger controller, a db node, a submitter, three workers, and two unmanaged ones.
Every node is a container with a CPU and memory limit. For a managed worker, Slurm is told exactly these numbers.
Memory covers the whole node: the jobs, its services and its temporary files. So raise it for jobs that need a lot.
In the slurm section, a block of text is added to the matching file: here slurm.conf and the cgroup config.
A map of named blocks becomes separate fragments instead, in a directory of their own.
So: one line is a complete config, limits are what Slurm sees, and a config is as trusted as a script.
Next up, the node definitions in detail. See you there!
